classes.why: ed3c/noodles#325 subsumes the repository's one concrete single-source rule. The admitted task model was previously guarded by noodles.validate_task_profile_single_source with an exemption list in policy/fitness.json; both are retired into this row, so one implementation judges every registered class.

projections.why: Noodle reads its own routing default before any noodles code runs, so it cannot resolve the pointer; the literal is the handoff to a process that does not read this policy.
The model-eval boundary names the execute model in the argv it refuses to spawn; the refusal has to carry the exact token it is refusing.

classes.why: The provider source URL is the identity half of a pinned external dependency. A second writer is how a retired provider survives in prose: the drift history this atom cites is provider pins copied into the README.

projections.why: The trusted provider-lock assertion compares the candidate's entries against a pinned list. ed3c/noodles#304 widened it for the staged compat removal and ed3c/noodles#301 retires it; until then the test is the admitted second reader, not a second writer.

classes.why: The exact 40-hex commit is what makes a provider pinned rather than floating. A copy that stops resolving to a live entry is the exact failure this detector exists to name.

projections.why: The context-closure source table cites the exact pinned bytes it read. It is a projection of the lock, and when the lock moves this row makes the citation say so instead of silently describing a commit nobody fetches.
The migration ledger records which pinned commit the skills-shared disposition was taken against; it is derived from the lock entry that still carries that commit.
Same trusted provider-lock assertion as the provider-source row, owned by the ed3c/noodles#304 -> #301 staged transition.

classes.why: The tree-sitter library and grammar commits. Registered with no projections on purpose: this class is the positive control that a clean class exists, so a green detector is not evidence that every class merely has a long exemption list.
